extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, appellants, respondents, and examiners involved in ex parte and inter partes reexamination appeals before the USPTO Board (PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural rules and content requirements for appeals (ex parte and inter partes reexamination) to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB), including examiner answers, new grounds of rejection, reply briefs, oral hearings, fees, remands, rehearing, and required contents of appellant and respondent briefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of examiner's answer (incorporation rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s answer is deemed to incorporate all of the grounds of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified by any advisory action and pre-appeal brief conference decision), unless the examiner’s answer expressly indicates that a ground of rejection has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner's answer should be read as carrying forward prior rejections unless expressly withdrawn; this affects what issues are properly before the Board and what must be addressed by appellant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner may include a new ground of rejection (definition and approval)
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner’s answer may include a new ground of rejection. Any rejection that relies upon any evidence not relied upon in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified by any advisory action) shall be designated by the primary examiner as a new ground of rejection. The examiner must obtain the approval of the Director to furnish an answer that includes a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate rejections based on evidence newly relied upon as 'new ground of rejection' and secure Director approval before including them in an examiner's answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's response options to a new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer exercise one of the following two options to avoid sua sponte dismissal of the appeal as to the claims subject to the new ground of rejection: (1) Reopen prosecution by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits or other evidence relevant to the new ground; or (2) Maintain appeal by filing a reply brief as set forth in § 41.41 addressing each new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request to reopen must include only evidence/amendments relevant to the new ground; filing amendments or evidence with a reply brief converts the filing into a request to reopen prosecution. Failure to act within two months risks dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and petition to seek designation of new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of the primary examiner’s failure to designate a rejection as a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer must be by way of a petition to the Director under § 1.181 filed within two months from the entry of the examiner’s answer and before the filing of any reply brief. Failure to timely file such a petition will constitute a waiver of any arguments that a rejection must be designated as a new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions to the Director to designate a new ground must be timely (two months) and precede any reply brief; otherwise arguments are waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of petition granted (designation granted) — prosecution reopened timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision granting a petition under § 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer will provide a two-month time period in which appellant must file a reply under § 1.111 to reopen the prosecution before the primary examiner. On failure to timely file a reply under § 1.111, the appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition is granted, appellant must timely file the § 1.111 reply within two months or face dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of petition denied (appeal maintained) — reply brief timing
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision refusing to grant a petition under § 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer will provide a two-month time period in which appellant may file only a single reply brief under § 41.41.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If petition denied, appellant gets a single two-month opportunity to file a reply brief; other filings may be barred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of petition by filing reply brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply brief under § 41.41 is filed within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer and on or after the filing of a petition under § 1.181 ... but before a decision on the petition, the reply brief will be treated as a request to withdraw the petition and to maintain the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a reply brief while a petition is pending effectively withdraws the petition and elects to maintain the appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief timing (single reply brief rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file only a single reply brief to an examiner’s answer within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner’s answer, or a decision refusing to grant a petition under § 1.181 to designate a new ground of rejection in an examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one reply brief is permitted and strict two-month timing applies measured from the later of examiner's answer or petition-decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief content restrictions (no new evidence/amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New amendments or evidence must be submitted by reopening prosecution; including them in a reply brief will convert the filing to a request to reopen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply brief argument scope limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any argument raised in the reply brief which was not raised in the appeal brief, or is not responsive to an argument raised in the examiner’s answer, including any designated new ground of rejection, will not be considered by the Board for purposes of the present appeal, unless good cause is shown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply briefs must be limited to issues previously raised or responsive to examiner's arguments; new issues risk exclusion absent good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extensions of time not generally applicable to appeal deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under § 1.136(a) of this title for patent applications are not applicable to the time periods set forth in several sections (e.g., reply brief, responses to examiner's answer, oral hearing requests). See § 1.136(b) for extensions to reply and § 1.550(c) for ex parte reexamination replies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume standard §1.136(a) extensions apply to PTAB appeal deadlines; consult the specific cross-referenced provisions for permissible extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal forwarding fee timing and failure consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant in an application or ex parte reexamination proceeding must pay the appeal forwarding fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(4) within the later of two months from the date of either the examiner’s answer, or a decision refusing to grant a petition under § 1.181. On failure to pay the fee within the period specified, the appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely payment of the specified fee is mandatory; non-payment causes dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: An oral hearing should be requested only in those circumstances in which appellant considers such a hearing necessary or desirable for a proper presentation of the appeal. An appeal decided on the briefs without an oral hearing will receive the same consideration by the Board as appeals decided after an oral hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve oral hearings for cases where they materially aid presentation; requesting a hearing does not guarantee additional substantive consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request form, timing, and fee
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file, as a separate paper captioned 'REQUEST FOR ORAL HEARING,' a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(3) within two months from the date of the examiner’s answer or on the date of filing of a reply brief, whichever is earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use separate paper with caption and include exact fee; adhere to the two-month deadline measured as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing evidence and argument reliance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: At the oral hearing, appellant may only rely on evidence that has been previously entered and considered by the primary examiner and present argument that has been relied upon in the brief or reply brief, except upon a showing of good cause, appellant and/or the primary examiner may rely on a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New evidence is generally barred at hearing; new arguments based on recent controlling decisions may be allowed upon showing good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral argument time limits and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If an oral hearing is held, oral argument will ordinarily be limited to twenty minutes for appellant and fifteen minutes for the primary examiner unless otherwise ordered. Appellant will argue first and may reserve time for rebuttal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise arguments to fit time limits; plan for rebuttal if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board decision types and remand effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board, in its decision, may affirm or reverse the decision of the examiner in whole or in part on the grounds and on the claims specified by the examiner. The Board may also remand an application to the examiner. Where a decision includes a remand, that decision shall not be considered final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmance on any ground generally results in general affirmance of that claim; remands keep the matter non-final for judicial review until conclusion of remand proceedings (unless later made final).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute examiner's answer after remand — appellant options
rubrics_metrics.description: If a substitute examiner’s answer is written in response to a remand by the Board, the appellant must within two months from the date of the substitute examiner’s answer either (i) Reopen prosecution by filing a § 1.111 reply with or without amendment or affidavits/evidence relevant to the remand, which will be entered and treated as request to withdraw the appeal; or (ii) Maintain appeal by filing a reply brief under § 41.41 (which, if accompanied by amendment/evidence, will be treated as a request to reopen).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After remand, act promptly within two months and be aware that submitting amendments/evidence converts appeal-maintaining filings into reopening requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may designate new ground of rejection in its decision
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Board has knowledge of any grounds not involved in the appeal for rejecting any pending claim, it may include in its opinion a statement to that effect with its reasons for so holding, and designate such a statement as a new ground of rejection of the claim. A new ground of rejection pursuant to this paragraph shall not be considered final for judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Board-designated new ground obliges the appellant to choose reopening or rehearing; the new ground binds the examiner unless overcome by amendment/new evidence not previously of record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant options when Board designates a new ground (remedy on new ground)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Board enters such a non-final decision, the appellant, within two months from the date of the decision, must either (1) Reopen prosecution by submitting amendment or new evidence relating to the rejected claims so they are reconsidered by the examiner (remand), or (2) Request rehearing under § 41.52, addressing the new ground of rejection and stating with particularity the points believed misapprehended or overlooked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely election between reopening and rehearing is required; reopening allows the examiner to reconsider, while rehearing challenges the Board's reasoning on the existing record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for review of undesignated new ground of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request to seek review of a panel’s failure to designate a new ground of rejection in its decision must be raised by filing a request for rehearing as set forth in § 41.52. Failure of appellant to timely file such a request for rehearing will constitute a waiver of any arguments that a decision contains an undesignated new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use rehearing to challenge failures to designate new grounds; timing is strict and waiver results from delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board may order additional briefing/information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may order appellant to additionally brief any matter that the Board considers to be of assistance in reaching a reasoned decision on the pending appeal. Appellant will be given a time period within which to respond to such an order. Failure to timely comply with the order may result in the sua sponte dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply promptly with Board-ordered supplemental briefing; non-compliance risks dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rehearing filing requirements and permitted new arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: Appellant may file a single request for rehearing within two months of the date of the original decision. The request must state with particularity the points believed to have been misapprehended or overlooked. Arguments not previously raised and evidence not previously relied upon are not permitted, except (i) a new argument based upon a recent relevant decision of either the Board or a Federal Court, (ii) new arguments responding to a new ground of rejection designated pursuant to § 41.50(b), and (iii) new arguments that the Board’s decision contains an undesignated new ground of rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearing is a narrow vehicle; specify precisely what was misapprehended and rely only on permitted categories of new arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action following Board decision — jurisdiction and further action
rubrics_metrics.description: After decision by the Board, jurisdiction over an application or patent under ex parte reexamination proceeding passes to the examiner, subject to appellant’s right of appeal or other review, for such further action by appellant or by the examiner as the condition of the application or patent may require to carry into effect the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-decision process returns matter to examiner for implementation unless further review is pursued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter partes appeal definitions (appellant, owner, requester, respondent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: Appellant means any party filing a notice of appeal or cross appeal under § 41.61. Owner means the owner of the patent undergoing inter partes reexamination. Requester means each party, other than the owner, who requested the inter partes reexamination. Respondent means any requester responding under § 41.68 to the appellant’s brief of the owner, or the owner responding under § 41.68 to the appellant’s brief of any requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify party roles and who may appeal or respond in inter partes reexamination appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of appeal and cross appeal timing and content (inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of a Right of Appeal Notice under § 1.953, the owner or requester may appeal to the Board within the time provided in the Right of Appeal Notice and paying the fee set forth in § 41.20(b)(1). Cross appeals may be filed within fourteen days of service of the other party's notice upon payment of fee. The notice must identify the appealed claim(s) and be signed. An appeal or cross appeal must be taken from all the rejections or determinations which the appellant proposes to contest. The time periods for filing a notice of appeal or cross appeal may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely file and sign the notice and pay fees; incomplete or untimely notices risk dismissal; identify all contested matters to avoid procedural issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-compliance cure period for notice of appeal (inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a notice of appeal or cross appeal is timely filed but does not comply with any requirement of this section, appellant will be notified of the reasons for non-compliance and given a non-extendable time period within which to file an amended notice. If appellant does not then file an amended notice within the set time period, or files a notice which does not overcome all reasons for non-compliance, that appellant’s appeal or cross appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a single non-extendable cure opportunity; failure to correct leads to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and affidavits/evidence after filing an inter partes appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after the date of filing an appeal canceling claims may be admitted where such cancellation does not affect the scope of any other pending claim. All other amendments filed after the date of filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by § 41.77(b)(1). Affidavits or other evidence filed after the date of filing an appeal will not be admitted except as permitted by reopening prosecution under § 41.77(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, post-appeal amendments/evidence are barred except narrow exceptions (e.g., claim cancellations or reopening per §41.77(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction over inter partes appeal file to Board and relinquishment/remand
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction over the proceeding passes to the Board upon transmittal of the file, including all briefs and examiner’s answers, to the Board. If the Board determines the file is not complete or not in compliance, it may relinquish jurisdiction to the examiner or take other action to permit completion. Prior to entry of a decision, the Director may sua sponte order the proceeding remanded to the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing the complete record transfers jurisdiction to the Board, but the Board or Director may relinquish or remand for completeness or other reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing briefs in inter partes appeals (strict non-extendable deadlines)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appellant’s brief must be filed no later than two months from the latest filing date of the last-filed notice of appeal or cross appeal (or two months after expiration of time if a party entitled to file fails to do so). Once appellant's brief is filed, any respondent brief must be filed within one month from service of the appellant’s brief. An appellant may file a rebuttal brief within one month of the examiner’s answer. The time for filing these briefs may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the tight, generally non-extendable schedule for appellant, respondent, and rebuttal briefs; court-style extensions are not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant's brief required contents (inter partes)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appellant’s brief shall contain the following items under appropriate headings and in the order indicated: (i) Real party in interest; (ii) Related appeals, interferences, and trials (identifying numbers and including copies of decisions in appendix); (iii) Status of claims; (iv) Status of amendments; (v) Summary of claimed subject matter (concise explanation of each independent claim with specification and drawing references, and identification of structure corresponding to any 35 U.S.C. 112(f) means-plus-function/step-plus-function elements with specification references); (vi) Issues to be reviewed on appeal; (vii) Argument with citations to statutes, regulations, authorities, and record; (viii) Claims appendix; (ix) Evidence appendix (copies of evidence submitted under §§1.130-1.132 or other evidence entered by the examiner and where entered in the record); (x) Related proceedings appendix (decisions); (xi) Certificate of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item must be included under proper headings and in order. For 112(f) elements identify corresponding structure/material/acts with exact specification citations. Failure to include these items or to comply may lead to dismissal after a non-extendable cure opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: No new amendments/evidence in appellant's brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief shall not include any new or non-admitted amendment, or any new or non-admitted affidavit or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New material must be presented only by permitted procedural mechanisms (e.g., reopening prosecution) — do not attempt to introduce it in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequence of non-compliant brief (notice and non-extendable cure)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a brief is filed which does not comply with all the requirements of the relevant sections, appellant will be notified of the reasons for non-compliance and given a non-extendable time period within which to file an amended brief. If appellant does not file an amended brief within the set time period, or files an amended brief which does not overcome all the reasons for non-compliance, that appellant’s appeal will stand dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a single, non-extendable cure window for brief defects; failure to cure results in dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's brief scope and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent(s) may file a respondent brief once within the time limit and must sign and pay the requisite fee. The respondent brief shall be limited to issues raised in the appellant brief to which the respondent brief is directed. The respondent brief shall contain items under headings similar to the appellant’s brief (real party in interest; related appeals; status of claims; status of amendments; summary of claimed subject matter; issues to be reviewed — accepting or disputing appellant's statements; argument with citations; evidence appendix; related proceedings appendix; certificate of service). If appellant’s statements are disputed, the errors must be specified with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent briefs must mirror structure and specify particular errors when disputing appellant statements. A requester respondent may not address briefs of other requesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix requirements (both appellant and respondent)
rubrics_metrics.description: An evidence appendix must contain copies of any evidence submitted pursuant to §§ 1.130, 1.131, or 1.132 or any other evidence entered by the examiner and relied upon by the party in the appeal, along with a statement setting forth where in the record that evidence was entered. Reference to unentered evidence is not permitted in the brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include only evidence that is of record and specify precise record locations; do not reference unentered materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and separate argument rules for claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If multiple claims subject to the same ground of rejection are argued as a group by appellant, the Board may select a single claim from the group to decide the appeal for the group on the basis of the selected claim alone. Failure to separately argue claims which appellant has grouped together shall constitute a waiver of any argument that the Board must consider the patentability of any grouped claim separately. Any claim argued separately should be placed under a subheading identifying the claim by number. A statement which merely points out what a claim recites will not be considered an argument for separate patentability of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If separate patentability is sought for specific claims, argue them separately under subheadings; mere recitation is insufficient and grouping can cause waiver.
